insights.concise_text: The Dual Decomposition (DD) based algorithm improved PP-attachment accuracy by 10% over the MSTParser baseline on 100 parallel sentences from the Hindi-English Tourism parallel corpus.

triple.subject: Dual Decomposition (DD) based algorithm
triple.object: MSTParser baseline by 10% on 100 parallel sentences

insights.concise_text: The DD algorithm enforces agreement between English and Hindi parse trees subject to word alignments, and its best PP-attachment result occurred at 30 iterations.

triple.subject: DD algorithm agreement constraints
triple.object: best PP-attachment result at 30 iterations

insights.concise_text: Because Hindi case markers waali and se make PP-attachment clear, the proposed approach uses parallel Hindi sentences to disambiguate English PP attachments.

triple.subject: Hindi case markers waali and se
triple.object: parallel Hindi sentences for English PP-attachment disambiguation

insights.concise_text: The DD algorithm's input is a parallel English-Hindi sentence pair with word alignments, while GIZA++ word-alignment errors may cascade and cause the system to underperform.

triple.subject: GIZA++ word-alignment errors
triple.object: DD algorithm using parallel English-Hindi sentence pairs with word alignments

insights.concise_text: The Project Algorithm predicts target-language trees using source-language parse trees and word alignments, and its projected paths are supplied by two classifiers in a pipeline.

triple.subject: Project Algorithm
triple.object: two classifiers in a pipeline for projected paths

insights.concise_text: The DD algorithm's projected-path score is the sum of edge scores, and the Project Algorithm's argmax maximization uses the score of the best projected path for all edges.

triple.subject: Project Algorithm argmax maximization
triple.object: projected-path score as the sum of edge scores

insights.concise_text: The DD algorithm was evaluated on 100 parallel sentences with manually annotated PP-attachment ambiguity, where it marked 64 attachments correctly in the best case.

triple.subject: DD algorithm
triple.object: 100 parallel sentences with manually annotated PP-attachment ambiguity

insights.concise_text: The baseline system is the attachment predicted by MSTParser models, and the MSTParser model correctly disambiguated 54 PP-attachments, giving 54% baseline accuracy.

triple.subject: MSTParser baseline
triple.object: 54 PP-attachments and 54% baseline accuracy

insights.concise_text: The DD algorithm initializes English and Hindi trees from MSTParser models, and the Coordinate Descent algorithm calls the Project Algorithm until convergence.

triple.subject: Coordinate Descent algorithm
triple.object: MSTParser-initialized English and Hindi trees

insights.concise_text: The path-length classifier predicts lengths 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5, while the path-prediction classifiers predict paths of length 2, 3, 4 and 5.

triple.subject: path-prediction classifiers
triple.object: path-length classifier outputs 2, 3, 4 and 5
